title: How Many Code and Test Cases Are Enough? Evaluating Test Cases Generation from a Binary-Matrix Perspective
year_venue: 2026 arXiv v3 (2026-03-25); journal/peer-reviewed venue not verified
datasets: TC-Bench: 877 English-language competitive-programming problems, 9,347 wrong submissions in final benchmark, and 7,016 accepted reference solutions; source corpus 2.23M submissions across USACO/IOI/ICPC. Hugging Face dataset has one `test` split with 877 rows; individual problems contain 3–56 wrong codes and rank field.
This paper does not use Defects4J, BugsInPy, or SWT-Bench experimentally; SWT-Bench is only cited in related work.
artifact_url: https://github.com/Luowaterbi/TC-Bench (data construction and evaluation code); https://huggingface.co/datasets/Luoberta/TC-Bench (877-row benchmark dataset, MIT card license).
license: HF dataset MIT card; no top-level software license
input_setting: Natural-language competitive-programming statement + optional correct reference code depending on method; output is generated test input(s) with expected outputs. Methods include CRUX, PSEUDO, ALGO, LiveCodeBench (LCB), and HumanTest (HT). Valid generated cases must pass selected accepted solutions, then are run on selected wrong submissions. This is algorithmic test generation, not repository-level unit-test generation or historical bug reproduction.
reproduction_grade: B (custom-model evaluation feasible with public benchmark/evaluator; exact paper replay conditional on generation prompts/API snapshots)
concept_hook: High for own-model test adequacy on diverse wrong-code signatures; complementary only for Java/Python root-cause issue task.
limitation: Algorithmic C++ benchmark; no issue reports or real repository bug history. Generator implementations/prompts absent from public source.
